title: Reservation oversubscription cascades across workflow services
context: Two independent workflow queue pools accept batch and reserved interactive workload. Each pool has a hard capacity allocation. Workload can appear low in a single dashboard because two allocations must be summed. Downstream endpoints can be isolated or multi-homed; assume no automatic capacity rebalancing.
semantics: queue-REGION is locally down if batch_jobs + interactive_reserved > capacity. Otherwise that queue is healthy. A batch request consumes one capacity unit, as does an interactive reservation; unused reservations still count. This is the only local fault. A dependent service follows needs_all/needs_any exactly.

hypotheses.description: Both queues are healthy because batch load alone fits their capacities.
The east queue exceeds capacity only after batch jobs and interactive reservations are combined.
The west queue is over-subscribed because 40 is greater than 60.
The coding agent fails independently of queue dependencies.

actions.meaning: Reduce east reserved interactive allocation to 20
Increase east pool hard capacity to 140

provenance: Inspired by real queue-throttling cascading failures including GitHub Actions 2025-06-05; all capacities, topology and demand data are invented.
